{{Short description|Aphorism}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=September 2021}}
'''"(There's) no such thing as a stupid question"''' is a common phrase. It implies that the quest for [[knowledge]] includes failure, and that just because one person may know less than others, they should not be afraid to ask rather than pretend they already know. In many cases, multiple people may not know, but are too afraid to ask the "stupid question"; the one who asks the question may in fact be doing a service to those around them.

==Origins==
==="There are no stupid questions"===
[[Carl Sagan]], in his work ''[[The Demon-Haunted World: Science as a Candle in the Dark]]'', said: "There are naïve questions, tedious questions, ill-phrased questions, questions put after inadequate self-criticism. But every question is a cry to understand the world. There is no such thing as a dumb question".

A 1970 [[Dear Abby]] column in ''[[The Milwaukee Sentinel]]'' said: "There is no such thing as a stupid question if it's sincere. Better to ask and risk appearing stupid than to continue on your ignorant way and make a stupid mistake.<ref name="Van Buren">{{Cite news |last=Van Buren |first=Abigail |date=3 December 1970 |title=Time Waits For No One |newspaper=[[The Milwaukee Sentinel]] |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=balRAAAAIBAJ&sjid=UxEEAAAAIBAJ&pg=7434,900282 |access-date=19 December 2013}}</ref>

"There is no such thing as a stupid question, only stupid answers".<ref name="books.google">{{Cite book |last=Weissman |first=Jerry |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QXCuAAAAQBAJ&q=%22no+such+thing+as+a+stupid+question%22&pg=PT184 |title=Presentation Skills That Will Take You to the Top (Collection) |date=22 August 2013 |isbn=9780133443011}}</ref> ''Presentation Skills That Will Take You to the Top'' says that within the business world, the adage holds true. The book adds "a question might be uninformed, tangential, or seemingly irrelevant, but, whether the presenter perceives it to be stupid or not, every audience member has every right to ask any sort of question".<ref name="books.google" />

''In the Line of Fire: How to Handle Tough Questions – When It Counts'' suggests that there are no stupid questions, rather there are "tangential questions", and that these should be dealt with swiftly and effectively.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Weissman |first=Jerry |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7SGDAAAAQBAJ&q=%22no+such+thing+as+a+stupid+question%22&pg=PT74 |title=In the Line of Fire: How to Handle Tough Questions – When It Counts |date=23 August 2013 |isbn=9780133157918 |access-date=27 September 2021 |archive-date=27 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210927030130/https://books.google.com/books?id=7SGDAAAAQBAJ&q=%22no+such+thing+as+a+stupid+question%22&pg=PT74 |url-status=live }}</ref>

''Designing Field Studies for Biodiversity Conservation'' says "there's no such thing as a stupid question, as long as it ends in a question mark".<ref>{{Cite book |last=Feinsinger |first=Peter |url=https://archive.org/details/designingfieldst0000fein |title=Designing Field Studies for Biodiversity Conservation |date=1 July 2001 |publisher=[[Island Press]] |isbn=9781559638784 |page=[https://archive.org/details/designingfieldst0000fein/page/147 147] |quote=no such thing as a stupid question. |url-access=registration}}</ref>

A variation of the phrase is once used by ''[[South Park]]''{{'}}s [[Mr. Garrison]]: "Remember, there are no stupid questions, just stupid people."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mobile.twitter.com/southpark/status/465925052181909504?lang=en|title="Remember there are no stupid questions, just stupid people." #MrGarrison #LifeLessons|website=Twitter.com|access-date=29 May 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.imdb.com/title/tt0705964/characters/nm0005295|title="South Park" Starvin' Marvin (TV Episode 1997) |website=IMDb.com|access-date=29 May 2022}}</ref>

==="There are stupid questions"===
The article ''Ink Out Loud: There's no such thing as a stupid question,' and other ailments lavender cures''<ref name="Feder">{{Cite web |last=Feder |first=Mandy |year=2013 |title=Ink Out Loud: There's no such thing as a stupid question,' and other ailments lavender cures |url=https://www.record-bee.com/2013/07/05/ink-out-loud-theres-no-such-thing-as-a-stupid-question-and-other-ailments-lavender-cures |url-status=live |newspaper=[[Lake County Record-Bee]] |location=[[Lake County, California|Lake County]]|access-date=23 August 2018 |archive-date=15 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210215033242/https://www.record-bee.com/2013/07/05/ink-out-loud-theres-no-such-thing-as-a-stupid-question-and-other-ailments-lavender-cures/ }}</ref> defines stupid questions as:
* Questions asked by someone who already knows the answer but is [[trolling]] the person they are asking.
* Questions of which the answer should be painfully obvious to any person with a pulse who has lived on this Earth for more than a decade.
* Questions that can be answered on one's own with complete certainty. After all, information found online or from other sources can be wrong, so it never hurts to check.
* Questions that include ridiculous or hypothetical assumptions. 
* Those questions that have already been answered, but the asker was not listening or paying attention.

Questions cited as stupid that were asked by the media pool at the [[2000 Super Bowl]] are "[[Ray Lewis]]? Yeah, Ray, how long have you been surrounded by thugs?", "If you were a tree, what kind of tree would you be?", and "Can you name [[the Backstreet Boys]]?"<ref name="Finder">{{Cite web |last=Finder |first=Chuck |date=22 January 2000 |title=The Big Picture: No such thing as a stupid question? |url=http://old.post-gazette.com/sports/columnists/20000121thebig.asp |newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] |access-date=19 December 2013 |archive-date=19 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131219223428/http://old.post-gazette.com/sports/columnists/20000121thebig.asp |url-status=dead }}</ref>

''Breaking into the Game Industry'' argues that the adage (and the related one "the only stupid question is the one that is never asked") is only relevant for the classroom and that in the real world when you want to try to impress someone, there are many stupid questions one can ask.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Brathwaite |first=Brenda |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=RYMLAAAAQBAJ&q=%22no+such+thing+as+a+stupid+question%22&pg=PA281 |title=Breaking into the Game Industry: Advice for a Successful Career from Those Who Have Done It |year=2011 |isbn=978-1435458055 |access-date=27 September 2021 |archive-date=27 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210927030159/https://books.google.com/books?id=RYMLAAAAQBAJ&q=%22no+such+thing+as+a+stupid+question%22&pg=PA281 |url-status=live }}</ref>

''School House Diary: Reflections of a Retired Educator'' notes that teachers are fond of saying this phrase, and suggests that while they themselves want to call out the stupid questions, they fall back on the adage in order to prevent the child from being ridiculed.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Roberts |first=Jerry L |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=q3qXGofdPO0C&q=%22no+such+thing+as+a+stupid+question%22&pg=PA122 |title=School House Diary: Reflections of a Retired Educator |date=20 July 2011 |isbn=9781462008186 |access-date=27 September 2021 |archive-date=27 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210927030120/https://books.google.com/books?id=q3qXGofdPO0C&q=%22no+such+thing+as+a+stupid+question%22&pg=PA122 |url-status=live }}</ref>
